gates.title: Per-image licensing, archive capture, and public availability
gates.reason: The still is a frame from Computer Chronicles episode 'Windows 95' (CC1301), which the Internet Archive item describes as 'Copyright 1995 Stewart Cheifet Productions.' The English-language item carries no licenseurl or rights field. The French-language version (fr_cc190_windows_95) carries CC BY-NC-ND 2.0, but that license is on a different item, and its NonCommercial and NoDerivatives terms may not fit a published YouTube video or a pillarboxed editorial frame. The on-stage event imagery (Windows logo, Start staging) is Microsoft's event design, and the report may include Microsoft-supplied event video; that underlying ownership is not documented. Evidence cannot settle fair use or permission, so the gate stays open as a rights review question. Nothing was cleared.

claims.claim: The frame depicts the Windows 95 launch event at Microsoft in Redmond, Washington.
evidence: The broadcast caption burned into the frame reads 'MICROSOFT / REDMOND, WA' (source/original.png).
CC1301 narration at 00:06:46: 'here's what it was like in Redmond, Washington the day Windows 95 was finally released' (IA ASR transcript, evidence/source-excerpts.md).
CC1301 narration at 00:06:58: 'Bill Gates invited Jay Leno to launch Windows 95 at this Hollywood-style event at Microsoft headquarters.'

The stage in the frame (Windows flag screens, 'Start' sign, lectern) matches the independent Microsoft/Caribiner launch tape on the Internet Archive (item microsoftwindows95launchwithbillgatesandjayleno1995, frames at 715 s and 4914 s). This is a visual cross-check only, not the basis of identification.
claims.identification_basis: source caption and narration, not appearance

evidence: Microsoft press release dated 21 August 1996 announces 'the one-year anniversary of the Windows 95 operating system on Saturday, Aug. 24' (https://news.microsoft.com/source/1996/08/21/one-year-anniversary-of-windows-95-to-be-celebrated/, accessed 2026-09-15).
The CC1301 narration says the footage is from 'the day Windows 95 was finally released' but gives no calendar date.

claims.claim: Publication: Computer Chronicles season 13 episode 'Windows 95', originally broadcast in 1995.
evidence: IA item description: 'Originally broadcast in 1995. Copyright 1995 Stewart Cheifet Productions.'

Wikipedia 'List of Computer Chronicles episodes' gives 26 September 1995 as the original release date (secondary source, accessed 2026-09-15). No primary broadcast log was found, so the exact air date is recorded as unverified.

claims.claim: SCRIPT.md:114 VISUAL: 'Windows 95 launch footage - the Rolling Stones, the lines outside CompUSA, the startup sound.'
evidence: CC1301 narration at 00:08:01-00:08:04 says the 'Start Me Up commercial' was previewed at the launch. That supports a Rolling Stones connection through the licensed song in the advertisement. It does not show a Stones appearance, and this still does not depict the Stones.
No examined source substantiates lines specifically outside CompUSA. The CC1301 item description says only 'stores opening at midnight.'
The startup sound is audio; this ticket carries no audio.
